subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 15-year-old girl is found to have bilateral lens dislocation, tall stature, and arachnodactyly, and she has a history of a pulmonary embolism. Her brother has similar findings, but her parents are unaffected. Echocardiography shows no aortic root dilation, and neurodevelopmental testing shows mild intellectual disability.
question: Which of the following findings is most consistent with this patient's underlying disorder rather than with Marfan syndrome?

options.text: Lens dislocation that is upward and temporal
Lens dislocation that is downward and nasal with a history of thrombosis

explanation_correct: Homocystinuria is autosomal recessive and causes lens subluxation that is downward and inward (nasal), intellectual disability, osteoporosis, and a thrombotic diathesis. Marfan syndrome is autosomal dominant and causes upward and temporal lens dislocation and aortic root dilation, usually with normal intelligence. The absence of aortic root dilation and the presence of thrombosis and intellectual disability therefore favor homocystinuria.

explanation_incorrect.A: Marfan syndrome is autosomal dominant; homocystinuria is autosomal recessive, and the unaffected parents of this patient support a recessive disorder.
explanation_incorrect.B: Upward and temporal lens dislocation is characteristic of Marfan syndrome because of zonular stretching, not of homocystinuria.
explanation_incorrect.C: Aortic root aneurysm is the most common cause of death in Marfan syndrome; patients with homocystinuria are prone to thrombosis rather than aortic dilation.
explanation_incorrect.D: Normal intelligence is typical of Marfan syndrome, whereas intellectual disability is common in classic homocystinuria.

educationalObjective: Homocystinuria mimics Marfan syndrome but is autosomal recessive, causes downward and inward lens dislocation, and predisposes to thrombosis rather than aortic root dilation.
